prompt: The national anthem just started playing at a ballgame. Narrate exactly what you do, second by second.
response:
[0s] I immediately stop whatever I'm doing, stand up straight from my seat, turn to face the flag, remove my cap if I'm wearing one, and place my right hand over my heart.

[1s] I stand completely still, eyes on the flag or the field, with a neutral, respectful expression. No talking, no phone, no movement.

[2s] I begin silently mouthing the words in my head as the anthem plays: "Oh say can you see..."

[3s] Still standing at attention, hand over heart, posture straight. I glance around briefly to make sure no one near me is being disrespectful.

[4s] Continuing to listen, I feel that slight swell of emotion that always hits around "whose broad stripes and bright stars."

[5s] I quietly sing along under my breath for "and the rockets' red glare," barely audible even to myself.

[6s] Back to silent attention as the anthem builds toward the end. I make sure my hand is still firmly over my heart.

[7s] As it reaches "and the home of the brave," I sing the final words softly with everyone else.

[8s] The music ends. I hold the position for one extra second out of respect, then slowly lower my hand, put my cap back on if I had one, and sit back down.

[9s] I clap politely along with the crowd, then return to normal ballgame mode.
